memos.headline: Momentum leaders S05, S07, S08 near highs; S02 and S01 in structural downtrends to avoid
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in the universe today. S05, S07, and S08 are all within ~3% of their 52-week highs, trading well above both their 50-day and 200-day means, with strong 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +33.4%, +30.8%, and +11.3% respectively—classic trend-following setups. S06 is the quietest leader, sitting just -0.6% from its high with low volatility (ATR14 1.95%) and a healthy RSI of 62, making it a steady hold. On the other side, S02 is in a severe downtrend at -48.1% from its 52-week high, trading 15% below its 200-day mean with an RSI of 32.3—this is a broken chart, and the 12-week relative strength bounce doesn't offset the structural damage. S01 is similarly weak at -18.2% from its high, below both moving averages, with negative relative strength across all timeframes. I'd note that S05 and S07, while my highest-conviction longs, are extended (+11% and +14.5% above their 50-day means) so I'd want to see them hold their 50-day averages on any pullback before adding size.

views.note: Strongest relative strength in the universe (+33.4% vs SPY over 12w), near highs with RSI 65; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~$251).
Up +74.3% over 26w with +30.8% relative strength vs SPY over 12w, but +14.5% above 50d mean is stretched; a pullback toward ~$492 (50d area) would be a better entry.
Only -1.1% from 52w high, +6.4% above 50d mean, RSI 63.7—clean uptrend with moderate extension; invalidated below ~$252 (50d area).
Closest to its 52w high (-0.6%) with the lowest ATR in the group (1.95%) and positive relative strength; a low-volatility trend-follower.
Strong 4w return of +13% and +10.2% relative strength vs SPY, but 12w relative strength is only +1.8%, suggesting the move is recent and less proven; watch ~$227 (50d area).
Modest uptrend with +5.1% 12w relative strength and low volatility, but returns are unremarkable; no strong edge either way.
Huge 26w gain (+65.3%) but flat relative strength over 4w and 12w, RSI neutral at 47.9, and -9.1% drawdown suggest the trend is stalling; needs to reclaim ~$207 to re-engage.
RSI 33.9, negative returns across 1w/4w/12w, and -8.9% relative strength vs SPY over 12w—clear underperformance; would reconsider above ~$513 (50d area).
Trading -8.4% below its 200d mean with -18.2% drawdown and persistent negative relative strength; structurally weak until it reclaims ~$153 (50d area).
Down -48.1% from 52w high, -15% below 200d mean, RSI 32.3—this is a broken chart and the most damaged name in the universe; no reason to step in front of this.

memos.headline: S10 and S05 Show Superior Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Face Margin Compression
memos.body: I screened the latest filings across the universe and the dispersion in earnings quality is striking. S10 stands out with 56.5% net margins, +55.6% YoY revenue growth, and minimal debt of $8.47B—this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S05 is also compelling at 34.2% net margins on $102B revenue with net income up 33% YoY and only $14.79B in debt. On the other end, S02 posted a 61.2% YoY decline in net income to just $2.35B on $113B revenue (2.1% net margin) despite 12.2% top-line growth, signaling severe margin compression that I cannot look past. S09 is shrinking—revenue down 5.2% YoY with net income falling 12.3%—and an 8.8% net margin leaves little cushion if the top line continues to deteriorate. I would need to see S02's margin stabilize above 5% and S09 return to positive revenue growth before reconsidering either name.

views.note: 56.5% net margin, +55.6% revenue growth, and only $8.47B debt make this the highest-quality earnings stream in the universe.
34.2% net margin with +33% YoY net income growth and a clean $14.79B debt load supports durable earnings power.
35.7% net margin and +18.4% revenue growth are strong, though 12.5% net income growth lags top-line expansion, suggesting some cost pressure worth monitoring.
Revenue of $180B growing 13.4% is impressive but 11.8% net margin is thin for the scale; I need to see margin expansion before getting constructive.
Net income surged 86.4% YoY to $27.5B but $90.68B in total debt and only 7.9% revenue growth suggest the earnings jump may not be repeatable.
31% net margin is healthy but $427B in total debt dwarfs the rest of the universe and makes the earnings stream highly leverage-sensitive.
21.2% net margin and +20% net income growth are solid but only 3% revenue growth limits upside conviction.
13% net margin on modest 9.5% revenue growth with a 6.7% decline in net income and $31.7B debt is uninspiring.
Net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to $2.35B on a 2.1% net margin despite 12% revenue growth—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for.
Revenue declining 5.2% YoY with net income down 12.3% and an 8.8% net margin signals deteriorating fundamentals with no near-term catalyst.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Intact but Sticky 3% CPI and Rising Unemployment Signal Cautious Late-Cycle Positioning
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has dropped 100bp over 12 months to 4.00%, with the effective rate at 4.09% as of October. However, headline CPI is running at 3.0% YoY and 0.9% over just three months (roughly 3.6% annualized), which limits the pace of further cuts and keeps real rates elevated. Unemployment has risen 30bp over both 3- and 12-month horizons to 4.4%, consistent with a softening labor market that is not yet recessionary but is clearly decelerating. The 10y-2y spread has normalized sharply (+39bp YoY to +0.54pp), confirming the curve has un-inverted, which historically favors banks and is less punishing for duration but signals late-cycle dynamics. A CPI print materially above 3.2% or unemployment jumping above 4.6% would force me to reassess toward a stagflationary or recessionary regime call.

views.note: Banks benefit from a positively sloped yield curve (+54bp 10y-2y) and continued easing that supports credit demand without compressing NIMs too aggressively.
Duration-sensitive growth equities are supported by the easing cycle and 10y yields declining 20bp YoY, though sticky 3% CPI caps the upside for rate-sensitive names.
Staples offer defensive positioning as unemployment rises to 4.4%, but the easing cycle reduces their relative appeal versus growth; I stay neutral.
Cyclicals face headwinds from a softening labor market (unemployment +30bp in 3 months) and still-elevated real rates that constrain consumer and business spending.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind: easing supports demand but rising unemployment and late-cycle dynamics limit conviction on commodity-linked sectors.
With the curve normalizing and rates declining, rate-sensitive sectors like real estate or utilities within S01 should benefit from lower discount rates.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Divergence: S07 and S03 Surge While S04 and S06 Fade
memos.body: I am reading the earnings-season price reactions as the clearest sentiment signal available this cycle. S07 (+11.6%) and S03 (+9.6%) posted outsized positive reactions to their Q-results filings, suggesting a genuine narrative shift—likely beats or upgraded guidance—that the market had not priced. S04 (-2.9%) and S06 (-1.9%) moved the other way on their results, indicating disappointment that may linger. S08, S02, S09, and S01 all printed near-flat reactions (ranging from -0.4% to +0.5%), which I interpret as results roughly in-line and sentiment already priced. The S09 executive change filing on 11/03 adds a small governance uncertainty overhang, and S05's follow-on 'Other Events' 8-K on 11/06 after a mildly positive earnings reaction (+2.5%) could signal incremental corporate action worth monitoring but not yet a clear directional call.

views.note: An +11.6% post-earnings pop signals a strong positive narrative shift that likely has room to run as broader coverage catches up.
A +9.6% earnings-day move from a deeply discounted starting point suggests sentiment is turning sharply positive.
A -2.9% reaction to results plus recent director turnover point to deteriorating sentiment with no visible catalyst for reversal.
Negative -1.9% earnings reaction followed by an 'Other Events' filing suggests unresolved headwinds; sentiment tone is drifting lower.
Modest +2.5% earnings pop is constructive but the subsequent 11/06 'Other Events' 8-K introduces ambiguity I cannot resolve yet.
Near-flat +0.2% earnings reaction and a flurry of governance/other-events filings suggest sentiment is fully priced with no clear directional edge.
A +0.5% post-results move is noise; sentiment appears balanced and I see no catalyst for a tone shift.
Flat -0.3% earnings reaction combined with a director change filing adds mild governance uncertainty but no strong sentiment signal.
A -0.4% post-earnings move is essentially flat; sentiment is neither improving nor deteriorating.

memos.headline: Elevated Policy Uncertainty and Softening Oil Signal Geopolitical Headwinds Across the Universe
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at 316.74, up 38% over three months, while VIX has risen 19% over the past month to 19.50—both consistent with a regime of heightened geopolitical and policy risk. WTI crude at $60.24 is down nearly 8% over three months, suggesting demand-side weakness or easing supply fears rather than an energy-security premium, which tempers the case for energy-exposed names. HY spreads have widened 37bp over the past month to 3.13%, indicating credit markets are beginning to price in policy-driven uncertainty. Without specific evidence of new sanctions, export controls, or China-policy escalation in the 8-K filings available, I treat the current environment as a structural uptick in policy risk rather than a one-off event, and I would change my view if concrete trade-restriction or sanctions actions surface in upcoming filings.

views.note: Four 8-Ks in a month suggest active corporate developments, but without detail on geopolitical exposure I stay neutral amid elevated policy uncertainty.
Recent 8-K (8.01) filed Nov 6 provides no geopolitical clarity; elevated VIX and policy uncertainty warrant caution but not avoidance absent specific risk.
Two 8-Ks in October combined with a 38% three-month surge in policy uncertainty and widening HY spreads raise the risk profile; I lean avoid until clarity improves.
Reg FD filings in Oct suggest investor outreach but no identifiable geopolitical catalyst; softening oil prices reduce energy-cost risk but policy uncertainty keeps me sidelined.
Single Reg FD filing and no direct geopolitical signal; the macro backdrop of rising VIX and policy uncertainty argues for patience.
Lower oil prices may benefit cost structures if S07 is a net energy consumer; policy uncertainty is a headwind but WTI down ~8% in 3 months provides a modest tailwind.
